title: Haters will say I am not actually a floating head and they can see my...
transcript: There are so many spooky shows in New York right now, so I'm appearing to you live as a spooky, disembodied head to tell you which ones I think you should see. Starting with Paranormal Activity. This is definitely the spookiest show on the list and really captures that feeling of watching a horror film live on stage. This show has some really cool effects to bring these scares to life. But honestly, where I think the show is most effective is playing on your paranoia. You are constantly on the edge of your seat, expecting something scary to happen, and sometimes it does, but a lot of times it doesn't, so it really keeps you on your toes. Next, we have A ghost in your ear, which is playing off Broadway. The thing that makes this one unique is that you're listening to the show through headphones. It is being recorded live by two actors in what looks like a sound booth. While there are a few visual scares, for the most part, it's all auditory. It kind of conjures the vibe of, like, sitting around a campfire and telling a spooky story, but they do a great job at building this soundscape that really feels immersive. And since it's a 90 minute no intermission, you're really locked in from start to finish. Finally, there's 2:22, A Ghost Story, which features a starry cast and is probably the most psychological of the three. Most interested in exploring the concept. Of ghosts, the nature of their existence, and if they even exist at all. Most of these scares here are jump scares, with a very loud, piercing, screaming sound effect, with a lot of the actual ghost activity happening off stage. So I definitely say this is the least scary of the three, but I do think it has the most interesting twist. One that I'm still not entirely sure worked for me, but will definitely leave you with a lot to talk about after.
classificationReason: Explicitly framed as a list of 'so many spooky shows in New York right now' covering Paranormal Activity, A Ghost in Your Ear (off-Broadway), and apparently more; a multi-show recommendation roundup.
